Subject: Procurement + Pricing path — Acme Corp (post-call recap)

Hi Samantha — great conversation earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has visibility: 

Summary of discovery:
- Primary use case: product search relevance + summarization for customer support (contains limited PII: names/email in support tickets).
- Expected traffic: POC ~50k tokens/day ramping to ~300k tokens/day in 6 months.
- Latency SLO: 200-400ms p95 for generate calls.
- Security: SOC 2 required, customer-controlled KMS would be preferred for Private but not mandatory for POC.

Procurement/commercial questions we discussed:
- Payment method: does Acme require PO/Net terms or will corporate card work for initial POC?
- Onboarding: vendor onboarding (W9, COI, signed SOW) — who on your side manages that?
- Marketplace: you mentioned interest in marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace) — is that a requirement or preference?

Packaging options & rough guidance:
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to get started (card or PO), on-demand billing, no infra management. Good for POC and early ramp.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity, commit-based pricing (monthly/annual), predictable unit costs and SLA. Recommended if you want throughput guarantees and predictable billing.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict compliance/data residency; includes KMS/HSM integrations and higher-touch onboarding.

Attached: Redwood-Pricing-Matrix-Acme-20260630.pdf (pricing bands for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Requests / next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement contact (name/email) and whether PO/Net terms are required from day 1. If PO required, please share standard onboarding checklist (W9, COI, security questionnaire owner).
2) Let us know if marketplace is preferred — we can prioritize an AWS Marketplace listing but that typically adds 2-3 weeks for listing and entitlements.
3) If you'd like, we can propose a Mutual Action Plan (timeline + milestones) once procurement path is confirmed.

If it helps, I can also loop in our solutions architect (David) and our sales lead (Aditya) to confirm a recommended configuration for POC vs committed deployment.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- Acme prefers to start with a PO/net-30 relationship for vendors. We can do a card to kick off a very small pilot but procurement will require a PO for any recurring/committed contract.
- Procurement contact: Tom Rivera (tom.rivera@acmecorp.com) — I've cc'd him. He runs vendor onboarding and will own legal/finance intake.
- Required docs: W9, signed SOW, SOC 2 report, and a completed security questionnaire. Tom will share our onboarding checklist shortly.
- Marketplace: We like the convenience of AWS Marketplace but it depends on price parity and whether you can offer the same commit discounts through Marketplace. If you can be listed, procurement can sometimes expedite approvals.

Architecture note: for the POC we prefer Hosted (to iterate quickly). For production we're leaning Dedicated if P95 latency and cost predictability are priorities — but if data residency/KMS is non-negotiable we may need Private. Could you confirm the delta in unit cost between Hosted on-demand vs a Dedicated 6-month commit in the pricing matrix?

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks for the fast reply and for looping Tom in. Answering your questions and adding a few specifics so procurement has what it needs: 

1) PO vs Card: 
- Pilot: We can accept a corporate card or an initial on-demand Hosted subscription to get the POC running in days.
- Production/Committed: If Acme requires PO/net-30 for recurring billing, we support PO-based billing and can issue monthly invoices against a PO. Invoices can be sent to procurement@acmecorp.com with Net-30 terms.

2) Marketplace: 
- AWS Marketplace: we can prioritize listing. Important to note: commit discounts are typically supported via Marketplace Private Offers — it adds ~2-3 weeks for setup and procurement needs to accept the private offer. Pricing parity can be arranged.

3) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (short):
- Hosted (API): Lowest friction. On-demand; unit price is higher at spot usage tiers but no infra commitments. Good for POC and early ramp.
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity with commit pricing; recommended when you want predictable unit economics and SLA-backed throughput. We offer tiered discounts at 3, 6, 12 month commits (example: 6-mo commit = ~18% off list in the attached matrix).
- Private: For strict compliance, brings higher TCO due to infra and onboarding; includes KMS integration. Best if you must manage keys or need an air-gapped option.

4) Documents we can provide now: SOC 2 Type II report redacted, standard W9, Draft SOW — attached (Draft-SOW-Acme-20260629.docx) and the Pricing Matrix. If procurement wants the full security questionnaire answered, David (solutions architect) can coordinate.

Next suggested steps:
- Tom: please confirm Acme onboarding checklist and whether you can accept a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace.
- If PO is required from day 1, let us know the PO contact for invoicing and any standard contract terms we should be aware of.
- If Acme wants to move to a Dedicated pilot, we can propose a 3-6 month pilot with a commit discount and a clear rollback/fallback to Hosted if throughput isn't reached.

I'm attaching the Draft SOW and the pricing matrix for reference. Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call to align with Tom and your procurement/finance folks.
